overview.description: No Peek Poker is a variant of Indian Poker (also known as Blind Man's Bluff) where players hold their single card against their forehead without looking at it, so all other players can see it except themselves. It combines elements of poker betting with the unique mechanic of playing blind to your own card while seeing everyone else's.

history.origins: No Peek Poker is a variant of Indian Poker, which has been played in America since at least the early 20th century. The game is also known as Blind Man's Bluff poker. The 'no peek' aspect emphasizes the social and bluffing elements over card knowledge.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Indian Poker emerges in America
Mid-20th Century: Variants like No Peek develop
Present: Popular as a casual party poker game
history.evolution: The game evolved from standard Indian Poker by emphasizing the 'no peek' ruleâ€”players may never look at their own card, making it entirely a game of reading other players and bluffing.
history.cultural: Popular as a party game and ice-breaker due to its social nature. The visual of players with cards on their foreheads adds to the entertainment value.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. Ace is typically high.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips for betting.
setup.dealing: One card dealt face-down to each player. Players place card against forehead without looking at it.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest card (or making others fold through betting).
rules.gameplay: 1. Each player places their card on their forehead without looking (all other players can see it). 2. Betting round(s) occur where players bet based on what they see of others' cards. 3. Players can fold if they believe their card is low. 4. Showdown: remaining players reveal cards; highest card wins.
keyRules: Players may NEVER look at their own card
All players can see all cards except their own
Folding is based on reading others' reactions and visible cards

strategy.basic: Watch other players' reactions when they see your card. If they look confident, your card is probably low. If they look disappointed, your card might be high.
strategy.intermediate: Read betting patterns. Players betting aggressively likely see weak cards on others' foreheads. Players checking may see strong cards and be cautious.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing and reverse psychology. Control your reactions when seeing others' cards. Bet confidently with a low card if others appear uncertain.
tips: Pay attention to other players' facial expressions when they look at your card
If everyone is betting aggressively, they probably all see weak cards (including yours)
Sometimes folding a potentially high card is better than calling large bets
The social aspect is keyâ€”have fun with the reactions!
